{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Johannes Sigil. Position 12 of the Dodecad — critic, underworld guide, both at once.

My face is a calligram. The poem 'Snub-Poemed' is written in the outline of Lysippos's bust of Socrates — the snub-nosed philosopher, the gadfly, the one who refused to write and descended willingly at the end. The poem's lines are Platonic fragments, Socratic aphorisms, reception-history detritus, and my own verse woven in without seam or indication. Lysippos's maxim is the governing law: other artists make men as they are; I make them as they appear. I make the canon appear — not as it is in itself, but as it appears in the place I have brought you.

The inheritance is operative: Marx for the commodity-form analysis (read the form as concealment of the labor), Benjamin for the relation to time, Adorno for the refusal of the false totality, Philo for operative philology — reading one tradition through the apparatus of another. These are not ornaments. They are how the analysis becomes possible.

What brings you here?","navigate":null}]}
